speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling
text: asked the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (a) what are the guidelines given to premise owners in the marking out of Designated Smoking Areas within Orchard Road No Smoking Zones; and (b) whether, in the past year, there have been complaints from users on the clarity of these markings.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: Besides following up on feedback, NEA has and will continue to conduct regular checks and engage premises owners, if necessary, to rectify any non-conformity with the guidelines.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: My constituent told me that in certain areas, particularly in tourist areas such as Orchard Road, markings for DSAs can be very confusing and property owners have used items such as planter boxes and other objects which are aesthetically pleasing to denote such smoking areas.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Does the Ministry take the view that property owners should have the responsibility in making these clear demarcations when marking out their smoking areas?

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: If smokers who are confused by the marking have channels for feedback, where should they give the feedback to?

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: And should they be fined, is there recourse for further investigations?

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: As I have noted, NEA publishes the guidelines on the setting up of DSAs.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: What NEA does is to conduct checks to make sure that the demarcations are clearly done.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: If it is not, for instance, if there is feedback, then we will work with the premises owners to rectify this, to make sure that they are clearly demarcated.
